page.layout: One page of text; marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, page number top right. Verse passages, headings, a woodcut ornament between sections, then a closing paragraph with a large initial.

p.i: Illic etiam videre queas quod supra mare est oppidum Aspendii op. Eurymedon fluuius.
Aspendum, fluminis iuxta vndas Eurymedontis, Vbi suum mactationibus Dianam placant. Horat. carm. lib.3.
Qui rore puro Castalia lauit Patara opp.
Dumeta, natalemque syluam, Delius, & Patareus Apollo.

main_text.head: Lycij montes, inter quos erat Chimæra.

p.i: Hic mouet Ortygia, mouet hic rapida agmina Nysa, Stat. Syl. li.1.
Hinc Lycij montes, gelidaque umbracula Thymbra. Hinc Lycia sortes. Virgil. Aeneid. lib.4.

main_text.head: Chimæra mons Lyciæ igniuomus, Capris, Leonibus & Draconibus abundans.

p.i: Prima leo, postrema draco, media ipsa Chimæra. Lucret.
Quoque Chimæra iugo mediis in partibus hirci, Ouid. lib.6. Meta.
Pectus & ora leæ, caudam serpentis habebat.
Ante leo, post autem draco, media autem capra, Homerus lib.6. Iliad.

main_text.head: PAMPHYLIA REGIO Asiæ Minoris maritima Lyciam sequitur.
main_text.p: ALia autem deinceps Pamphyliæ sunt vrbes, Dionysius. Corycus, Pergaque, & ventosa Phaselis. Corycus op. Perga opp. Phaselis op.

p.i: Harum autem ad Orientem mediam terram habitant Periti in bellis Lycaones, curuis arcubus vtentes.
— medio pelago Pamphilia puppi Luc. lib.8.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament between the Lycia and Pamphylia sections. Marginal notes on the right were transcribed as printed; the left margin is blank except for faint show-through. Several words in the margin notes and the opening verse lines are faint and may contain small errors (e.g. "Aspendum", "Lycij", "Pectus"), and the heading line "Asiæ Minoris" is partly broken by the initial.
